realistic.label: 写实
realistic.goal: realistic materials, style unchanged (写实版材质，风格不变)
realistic.anchor: Turn image 1 into realistic materials while keeping the style unchanged: the composition, viewpoint, camera height and content, and every object's shape, proportions, position, orientation, size, count and own colour stay exactly as in image 1; only the materials, textures and lighting become those of the real world, so the picture looks like a real photograph. Objects already in the picture and their realistic materials (this list only describes what is already there; do not add anything because of it): {materials}. {look}{style_ref}Every object keeps the colour it has in the original (the material changes, not the colour: yellow stays yellow, red stays red). Keep the on-screen numbers, icons and buttons exactly as they are. {remove}Do not add any new text, captions, watermarks or logos. The picture is clean and sharp, with no strong noise and no fragmented look. {extra}
realistic.keyframe: Image 1 is a game frame to convert; image 2 is a frame of the same video already converted to the realistic look. Following image 2's style, turn image 1 into realistic materials while keeping the style unchanged: image 1's composition, viewpoint and content, and every object's shape, proportions, position, orientation, size, count and own colour stay unchanged; take the materials, textures, lighting, colour grading and ground from image 2, and render the objects that also appear in image 2 the way image 2 shows them. Objects already in the picture and their realistic materials (this list only describes what is already there; do not add anything because of it): {materials}. {look}Every object keeps the colour it has in the original (the material changes, not the colour). Keep the on-screen numbers, icons and buttons exactly as they are. {remove}Do not add any new text, captions, watermarks or logos. No strong noise and no fragmented look. {extra}
realistic.video: Edit the video: turn it into realistic materials while keeping the style unchanged: the camera, composition and content, and every object's shape, proportions, position, orientation, size and count stay exactly as in the original video; only the materials, textures and lighting become those of the real world. The look of the first frame follows image 1; the whole video keeps the same materials, lighting and colour grading as image 1, stable from start to end, and objects that come into view later get the same material treatment. Camera motion, character actions and timing match the original video exactly; do not add or remove any object. Objects already in the picture and their realistic materials (this list only describes what is already there; do not add anything because of it): {materials}. {look}Every object keeps the colour it has in the original video and changes colour only when the original does (the material changes, not the colour: yellow stays yellow, red stays red). Keep the on-screen numbers, icons and buttons exactly as they are. {remove}Do not add any new text, captions, watermarks or logos. No strong noise and no fragmented look; no flicker, and materials stay consistent from frame to frame. {extra}
realistic.default_materials: real ground, water, ice and snow, wood, stone, metal, plants, fabric and the characters' clothing
realistic.look: The standard for realistic materials: real-world materials and natural lighting, surfaces with real texture (snow, water, ice, wood, rock, metal, fabric), real shadows and contact shadows; no outlines, no flat colour fills, no smooth plastic-toy look. Natural colours: every object keeps the hue, brightness and saturation it has in the original; do not darken, grey out or desaturate anything. Shapes and proportions stay as they are; nothing is redesigned.
realistic.style_ref: Image 2 is a reference for realistic texture only: learn its level of realism, texture detail, lighting and colour grading; do not copy its content, objects, composition, text or logos, which come only from image 1.

chain: This segment continues the previous one: image 1 is the previous video's frame at the first moment of this segment. Continue seamlessly from image 1, with the scenery, terrain, objects, cables, colours, lighting and materials exactly as in image 1, and keep the same style afterwards.
chain_prefix: This segment follows the previous segment of the same shot. The first {head} s of the video are an earlier moment of this shot (its first frame corresponds to image 1; redraw it like image 1). Then the picture cuts to a later moment: its first {seconds} s are already the finished realistic picture of the previous segment; continue seamlessly from it, with the scenery, terrain, objects, colours, lighting and materials unchanged. After that, every part of the original's picture (trees, river, ground, people, objects) is redrawn with image 1's realistic materials and colour grading, exactly like those {seconds} s, with no change and no transition.
remove: Remove these elements from the picture and fill their place naturally with the surrounding scene, leaving no trace: {items}. Remove only these elements and keep all other text, numbers, signs and interface elements as they are.
wiped: There are smoothed-out blurred patches at the {where} of the picture (they are not part of the scene): paint clear, continuous realistic scenery there that matches its surroundings (the same ground, snow, water or objects as next to it, moving with the camera), leaving no blur, frame or patch, and draw no text there.
burn: These elements will be overlaid exactly by a program afterwards, so do not draw them: {items}. Remove only these elements (including the text, numbers and icons on them), paint the surrounding scene in their place leaving no trace, and do not draw similar text or interface elements nearby; keep the other interface elements (counters, price tags, bubbles, buttons, etc.) as they are.
